summary.headline: ABSL AMC Q1 FY27 profit after tax rose 12% YoY to ₹309 crore on revenue of ₹625 crore; total AUM crossed ₹10 lakh crore after EPFO mandate.
summary.overview: Revenue grew 11% YoY to about ₹625 crore, PBT rose 9% to ₹406 crore and PAT rose 12% to ₹309 crore. Average AUM including alternates reached ₹6.28 lakh crore (up 42% YoY), inflated by the EPFO and ESIC mandates, and closing AUM crossed ₹10 lakh crore. Core mutual fund average AUM grew only 6% YoY to ₹4.28 lakh crore, with a marginal SIP book decline and May fixed-income outflows that reversed by June end. Management highlighted banking-channel recommendation-list wins and passive/ETF growth.

financial_highlights.change: +11% YoY vs ₹565 crore in Q1 FY26
Crossed milestone after EPFO mandate (about ₹6.08 lakh crore)

financial_highlights.metric: Equity mutual fund quarterly average AUM
financial_highlights.value: About ₹1.99 lakh crore (₹1,98,722 crore per CFO)

financial_highlights.change: Up about ₹28,650 crore vs Q1 FY26 base
Marginal reduction in SIP book per management

financial_highlights.value: 1.11 crore folios; about 40 lakh SIP-account folios
ESOP cost about ₹10 crore per quarter additional

segments.name: Mutual fund (active)
segments.commentary: Quarterly average AUM ₹4.28 lakh crore (+6% YoY); equity ₹1.99 lakh crore (+10% YoY). Flagship core funds (Flexi Cap, BAF, Multi Cap, Small Cap, Mid Cap, Multi Asset) seeing improved flows per management.

segments.name: Passive / ETF
segments.commentary: Passive average AUM about ₹40,000 crore (+14% YoY), folios 17.4 lakh, 52 products; ETF AUM +47% YoY. New passive head Hemen Bhatia appointed. Apex SIF Hybrid Long Short fund launched, two more SIFs planned.

segments.name: Alternates (PMS, AIF, GIFT City, real estate)
segments.commentary: PMS and AIF assets nearly ₹2 lakh crore including EPFO flows. Contribution about 7% of gross revenue and about 4% of net revenue after distributor payouts. Real estate AUM ₹700 crore; new ABSL Select Sector Fund and GIFT City retail licence obtained.

guidance_outlook: Yields to hold broadly flat (±1-2 bps) with telescoping pricing as AUM grows; equity yield about 63-64 bps, debt 24-25 bps, liquid 12-13 bps, ETF about 8 bps.
Employee cost expected to stay in the Q1 range going forward, including ESOP; other opex to rise at normal inflation with no cost shocks identified.
Alternates revenue contribution expected in a similar range going forward, ±1-2%.
Fee and commission expense expected to grow in line with alternates revenue.
PMS long-only target of about ₹20,000-21,000 crore over three years; AIF credit and money market funds targeted at ₹5,000-7,000 crore each to start.
Passive margins may be lower, but absolute profit expected to rise.
capex_capacity: Launch of retail GIFT City products (emerging market equity, India growth fund, global index funds) planned in the upcoming quarter.
Two more SIFs (equity long short, equity ex-top 100 long short) in preparation.
Fundraising underway for ABSL Select Sector Fund and Aditya Birla Real Estate Credit Opportunities Fund Series II.
Seed commitment up to 10% of fund size from AMC P&L for AIF credit funds, plus bridge financing for deals.
demand_pricing: Industry: quarterly average AUM ₹83.14 lakh crore (+15% YoY); June SIP ₹31,780 crore (+17% YoY); Q1 industry NFOs about ₹4,759 crore; SIP flows showed marginal slowdown.
Company SIP book June 2026 ₹1,085 crore; SIP AUM about ₹87,000 crore; SIP contribution about ₹3,300 crore for the quarter, flat vs Q4 per CFO.
May 2026 fixed-income outflows (duration-based liquid and non-liquid categories) hit average AUM; money returned by June end and July.
ELSS saw outflows and higher SIP cancellations; industry cancellation rates were higher than the previous quarter.
Banking distribution: products added to recommendation lists at HDFC Bank, Kotak, YES Bank/YES Securities, Standard Chartered; April strong, May and June muted per management.
Commission structure revised from 1 April 2026 (BER), described as neutral for AMC and distributors.

qa_highlights.question: Is the yield increase due to the TER regulation, and what are segment yields?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said the TER change took effect 1 April 2026 and was fully rolled out; Q1 yield reflects the true level. Equity 63-64 bps, debt 24-25 bps, liquid 12-13 bps, ETF about 8 bps.

qa_highlights.question: Why did employee expense rise, and is there a one-off?
qa_highlights.answer: Increase mainly from ESOP rolled out in January 2026, about ₹10 crore per quarter; quarterly employee cost expected to stay in the same range.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the commission restructuring went to distributors?
qa_highlights.answer: No specific bps split given; management said the revision was kept broadly neutral for AMC and distributors.

qa_highlights.question: Why was SIP market share lost?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to ELSS outflows and higher cancellations, plus May fixed-income volatility; flagship funds show improving SIP registrations and drive.

qa_highlights.question: Which funds are expected to see the most flows?
qa_highlights.answer: Flexi Cap first, then Balanced Advantage, Multi Asset Allocation and Small Cap; Mid Cap and thematic/value funds are secondary.

qa_highlights.question: What is the annualized revenue from ESIC and EPFO mandates?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said ESIC revenue is very marginal; the mandates mainly open the door to private EPFO flows, with outreach to about 1,350 EPFO clients.

risks_watch: Flow momentum weakened in May and June after a strong April; sustaining banking recommendation-list gains is key.
SIP book shrinking marginally; ELSS redemptions and higher cancellations could persist.
Headline AUM is inflated by the EPFO and ESIC mandates, with low revenue contribution; underlying mutual fund AUM grew only 6%.
Monsoon risk (below-normal rain forecast with El Niño) and West Asia-related import cost pressure on markets.
Passive margin dilution as telescoping pricing applies; alternates target execution (PMS, AIF, GIFT City).
summary.management_tone: Confident on franchise, product wins and passive/alternates growth, but cautious and somewhat defensive on SIP share loss, the May outflows and the commission restructuring details, which were answered without specific numbers.
key_quotes: So, the yield, what is there in Q1, reflects the true picture and will be maintained going forward in these levels.
Though we have seen this quarter a marginal reduction in the SIP book, something we continue to remain a big focus area to drive to the next level of growth momentum.
In fact, all the money has come back in June end and July.

adds.what: GIFT City retail products launch (emerging market equity, India growth fund, global index funds)
Two more SIFs (equity long short, equity ex-top 100 long short) in preparation

growth.why: No explicit top-line growth guidance; management guides yields flat (±1-2 bps), employee cost flat at Q1 run-rate and alternates contribution stable, with PMS target of ₹20,000-21,000 crore over three years and new SIF/GIFT City launches, but backing is partial and core MF AUM grew only 6% YoY.

mgmt.note: Hemen Bhatia appointed as new passive head; brief does not state the date or detail a specific growth plan beyond launches.
